methods.name: PreFT
methods.full_name: Prefill-only Finetuning (prefill-only LoRA, \( \text{LoRA}_P \), and prefill-only DiReFT, \( \text{DiReFT}_P \))
methods.paper_title: PreFT: Prefill-only finetuning for efficient inference
methods.formula_latex: h_i=W_0x_i+m_i\,\tfrac{\alpha}{r}BAx_i\ \ (\text{LoRA}_P),\qquad h^{(l)}_i\leftarrow h^{(l)}_i+m_i\,s_r\,W_2^{\top}\big(W_1h^{(l)}_i+b\big)\ \ (\text{DiReFT}_P),\qquad m_i=\mathbf{1}[\,i\le\ell\,];\ \ B\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}\times r},\ A\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times d_{in}},\ W_1,W_2\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times d},\ b\in\mathbb{R}^{r},\ s_r=1/\sqrt{r},\ \alpha=32;\ \ \text{decode positions } i>\ell \text{ run the frozen model and see the adapter only through the KV cache of positions } \le\ell;\ \ W_0\ \text{frozen},\ (A,B)\ \text{or}\ (W_1,W_2,b)\ \text{trained}
methods.trainable_params: r(d_{in}+d_{out})\ \text{per adapted matrix for LoRA}_P\ (\text{same as LoRA});\ \ L\,(2rd+r)\ \text{per model for DiReFT}_P\ (\text{one residual-stream intervention per layer})
methods.locus: Token-time locus: only the prompt positions \( i\le\ell \) processed at prefill, never the generated tokens. \( \text{LoRA}_P \) targets \( W_q,W_k,W_v,W_o,W_{gate},W_{up},W_{down} \) at every layer; \( \text{DiReFT}_P \) edits the residual stream after every block (post-MLP). Generated tokens reach the adapter only through the keys and values cached at prompt positions.
methods.structure: A position mask placed on an existing adapter. Writing an adapter as \( \langle\Phi_\phi,\mathcal F,\mathcal P\rangle \) (intervention, target modules, target positions), PreFT keeps \( \Phi_\phi \) and \( \mathcal F \) and shrinks \( \mathcal P=\{1,\dots,\ell+T\} \) to \( \mathcal P=\{1,\dots,\ell\} \). For \( \text{LoRA}_P \) the per-token update is the rank-\( r \) matrix \( m_i\tfrac{\alpha}{r}BA \), so the effective weight depends on the token: \( W_0+\tfrac{\alpha}{r}BA \) on prompt tokens and \( W_0 \) on generated tokens. For \( \text{DiReFT}_P \) the per-token update is a rank-\( r \) affine edit \( s_rW_2^{\top}(W_1h+b) \) of the residual stream at prompt positions. Attention is causal, so the whole effect on token \( i>\ell \) is carried by the adapted \( (K,V) \) entries of positions \( \le\ell \) at every layer. No KV entries are added, unlike prefix or KV-cache tuning.
methods.mergeable_reason: The update is gated by position, so no single matrix \( W' \) reproduces it: prompt tokens need \( W_0+\tfrac{\alpha}{r}BA \) and generated tokens need \( W_0 \). A single-adapter deployment could prefill with a merged copy and decode with \( W_0 \), but that doubles weight memory and defeats multi-adapter batching. The design goal is that decode runs the bare base model, so no adapter weights are touched at decode.
methods.identity_at_init: Yes. \( \text{LoRA}_P \) keeps LoRA's init (Kaiming-uniform \( A \), \( B=0 \), scaling \( \alpha/r \)). \( \text{DiReFT}_P \) uses the paper's zero-delta init \( W_1=0 \), \( b=0 \), \( W_2 \) with orthonormal rows (App. C.1 and the released preft/adapters/direft.py), so \( \Phi(h)=h \) at step 0. App. A.2 states the roles the other way round (orthonormal down-projection, zero up-projection and bias); either assignment gives a zero delta at init.
methods.key_idea: Multi-adapter serving is throughput-bound at decode, where each request's adapter matmul is memory-bound, so PreFT applies the adapter only to the \( \ell \) prompt tokens processed at prefill and runs every decode step on the frozen base model. The adapter steers generation only through the KV cache it shaped during prefill, and the method optimises accuracy per unit of serving throughput rather than per parameter.
methods.results_note: Serving 512 adapters on Llama 3.1 70B (4 H100s, Punica workload, vLLM fork), prefill-only DiReFT reaches 1.9x and prefill-only LoRA 1.87x the throughput of all-position multi-LoRA, while on RLVR (GSM8K, MATH, HumanEval) prefill-only adapters trail all-position ones by a mean of about 2 points.

relations.note: \( \text{LoRA}_P \) is LoRA with its parametrisation and init unchanged, restricted to prompt positions

\( \text{DiReFT}_P \) is ReFT's DiReFT variant applied to all prompt positions (ReFT uses a few prefix/suffix positions), with a new zero-delta init and a \( 1/\sqrt r \) prefactor for learning-rate transfer across ranks

mirror-image position masks on the same LoRA update: aLoRA is off for the prompt and on from the invocation sequence onward (to reuse the base model's prompt KV cache), PreFT is on for the prompt and off for generation (to drop adapter cost at decode); PreFT cites aLoRA as prior position-masked LoRA

both adapt a model through the KV cache seen at decode; Cartridges adds trained KV entries (extra attention work at every decode step), PreFT adds none and only reshapes the prompt's own cache; the paper calls KV-cache methods complementary and does not benchmark them

methods.name: OrthoMerge
methods.formula_latex: \text{OFT experts: } W_i=W_0R_i^{\top},\ R_i=(I+Q_i)(I-Q_i)^{-1},\ Q_i^{\top}=-Q_i;\ \ \text{other experts: } R_i^{\top}=U_iV_i^{\top},\ U_i\Sigma_iV_i^{\top}=\mathrm{SVD}\big(W_0^{\top}W_i^{\mathrm{tgt}}\big)\ \big(\text{Procrustes } \min_{R^{\top}R=I}\|W_i^{\mathrm{tgt}}-W_0R^{\top}\|_F\big),\ Q_i=(R_i-I)(R_i+I)^{-1};\ \ Q_m=\frac{\sum_i\|Q_i\|_F}{\|\sum_iQ_i\|_F}\cdot\frac{1}{N}\sum_{i=1}^{N}Q_i,\ \ R_m=(I+Q_m)(I-Q_m)^{-1};\ \ W_m=W_0R_m^{\top}+\mathrm{EuclidMerge}\big(\{\rho_i\}\big),\ \rho_i=W_i-W_0R_i^{\top}\ (\rho_i=0\ \text{for OFT experts});\ \ W_i^{\mathrm{tgt}}\in\{W_i,\ W_0+\tau_i^{\mathrm{conf}}\};\ \text{training-free, all weights frozen}
methods.trainable_params: 0\ (\text{training-free});\ \text{merge state per matrix: } N \text{ generators } Q_i\in\mathfrak{so}(d_{in})\ (\text{block-diagonal for OFT experts}) \text{ and, for non-OFT experts, residuals } \rho_i\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}\times d_{in}}
methods.locus: Weights of every linear layer of the merged experts: the input-side rotation of OFT-adapted layers, or, through orthogonal-residual decoupling, every layer of LoRA or fully fine-tuned experts (Llama-3.1-8B, Qwen2.5-3B, Llama-3.2-3B MergeBench experts, Qwen2.5-VL-7B). Post hoc, no training.
methods.structure: Merging in the Cayley chart of the orthogonal group. Each expert contributes a rotation \( R_i\in O(d_{in}) \), read off an OFT checkpoint or obtained by orthogonal Procrustes from \( W_0 \) to a target weight. The inverse Cayley map sends it to a skew-symmetric generator \( Q_i\in\mathfrak{so}(d_{in}) \); the generators are averaged linearly and rescaled by \( c=\sum_i\|Q_i\|_F/\|\sum_iQ_i\|_F\ge1 \) to undo norm loss from cancellation, then mapped back by the Cayley map. The merged multiplicative factor is exactly orthogonal, so \( W_0R_m^{\top} \) keeps the singular values of \( W_0 \) (hence its spectral norm and hyperspherical energy) for any number of experts. For non-OFT experts each weight is split as \( W_i=W_0R_i^{\top}+\rho_i \) (orthogonal plus residual), and the residuals are merged by a Euclidean rule (TA, TIES or TSV-M). The Procrustes target is \( W_i \) (OrthoMerge-G) or \( W_0+\tau_i^{\mathrm{conf}} \), where \( \tau_i^{\mathrm{conf}} \) keeps only the output-neuron rows of \( \tau_i=W_i-W_0 \) whose cosine with the mean task vector is negative (OrthoMerge-C). The Cayley chart covers only orthogonal matrices without eigenvalue \( -1 \), so a reflection returned by Procrustes would fall outside it; the paper does not discuss this case.
methods.mergeable_reason: The output is an ordinary weight matrix \( W_m=W_0R_m^{\top}+\rho_m \) in the base architecture (the merged OFT rotation can be multiplied into \( W_0 \)), so the merged model has no inference overhead.
methods.identity_at_init: Not applicable (training-free merge). Trivially consistent: if every expert equals \( W_0 \) then \( Q_i=0 \), \( R_m=I \), \( \rho_i=0 \) and \( W_m=W_0 \) (taking \( c=1 \) when \( \sum_iQ_i=0 \)).
methods.key_idea: Average OFT rotations in their Lie algebra rather than in weight space: map each \( R_i \) to \( Q_i\in\mathfrak{so}(d_{in}) \) with the inverse Cayley transform, average with a norm-restoring factor, and map back, so the merge stays on \( O(d_{in}) \) and preserves the spectrum of \( W_0 \). An orthogonal-plus-residual split by Procrustes extends the rule to LoRA and fully fine-tuned experts.
methods.results_note: Merging five OFT-finetuned Llama-3.1-8B experts (math, code, ScienceQA, CommonsenseQA, Social-IQA), OrthoMerge reaches 46.25% average task accuracy, above the experts' own 44.71% and every Euclidean baseline (TA, TIES, DARE, TSV-M), with the best out-of-domain average (41.80% on M-ARC and AGIEval).

methods.name: PRISM
methods.full_name: Projected Riemannian Invariant Subspace Mechanism (gauge-invariant tangent-space DP-LoRA)
methods.paper_title: PRISM: Gauge-Invariant Tangent-Space Differentially Private LoRA
methods.formula_latex: W=W_0+BA,\ B\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}\times r},\ A\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times d_{in}};\ \ \mathcal{P}_{B,A}(G)=G-(I-\Pi_B)\,G\,(I-\Pi_A),\ \ \Pi_B=B(B^{\top}B)^{\dagger}B^{\top},\ \Pi_A=A^{\top}(AA^{\top})^{\dagger}A;\ \ \widehat{\Delta Z}=\frac{1}{b}\sum_{i=1}^{b}\min\!\Big(1,\frac{C}{s_i}\Big)\mathcal{P}_{B,A}(G_i)+\frac{\sigma C}{b}\,\mathcal{P}_{B,A}(\Xi),\ \ G_i=\nabla_{\Delta W}\ell_i,\ s_i=\Big(\sum_{\text{modules}}\|\mathcal{P}_{B,A}(G_i)\|_F^2\Big)^{1/2},\ \Xi\sim\mathcal{N}(0,I_{d_{out}\times d_{in}});\ \ BA\leftarrow\mathrm{Retr}_r\big(BA-\eta\,\mathcal{A}(\widehat{\Delta Z})\big),\ \mathrm{Retr}_r=\text{truncated rank-}r\text{ SVD},\ \mathcal{A}=\text{Adam-style first moments of the noisy factor lifts, preconditioned by }(V+\lambda I_r)^{-1/2}\text{ from }r\times r\text{ second moments, with DP-aware floors }\lambda;\ \ W_0\ \text{frozen},\ (A,B)\ \text{trained}
methods.trainable_params: r(d_{in}+d_{out})\ \text{per adapted matrix (as LoRA)};\ \text{optimizer state: first moments of size } r(d_{in}+d_{out}) \text{ and two } r\times r \text{ second-moment matrices per module}
methods.locus: Any LoRA-adapted linear layer (experiments: \( W_q,W_k,W_v,W_{up},W_{down} \) of Gemma-3-4B-pt, Gemma-2-9B, Gemma-3-12B-pt). The method changes how per-example gradients are clipped and noised and how the factors are updated, not the adapter shape.
methods.structure: Plain LoRA on the fixed-rank manifold \( \mathcal M_r \), with DP-SGD moved from the factors to the base of the gauge bundle \( (B,A)\mapsto BA \), whose fibres are the orbits \( (B,A)\sim(BR,R^{-1}A) \), \( R\in GL(r) \). Per-example gradients are projected onto the tangent space \( T_{BA}\mathcal M_r=\{\delta B\,A+B\,\delta A\} \) (dimension \( r(d_{in}+d_{out}-r) \)) by \( \mathcal P_{B,A} \), which depends only on \( \mathrm{col}(B) \) and \( \mathrm{row}(A) \) and is therefore gauge invariant. The projection is lifted to the factors canonically as \( \Delta B=g_B(AA^{\top})^{\dagger}-\tfrac12\Pi_Bg_B(AA^{\top})^{\dagger} \), \( \Delta A=(B^{\top}B)^{\dagger}g_A-\tfrac12(B^{\top}B)^{\dagger}g_A\Pi_A \) with \( g_B=GA^{\top} \), \( g_A=B^{\top}G \), so that \( \Delta B\,A+B\,\Delta A=\mathcal P_{B,A}(G) \). Clipping uses the intrinsic Frobenius norm summed over all modules. The noise is the tangent projection of an isotropic Gaussian, sampled through factor lifts \( \Xi_B=(I-\Pi_B)\Omega_B(AA^{\top})^{-1/2} \), \( \Xi_A=(B^{\top}B)^{-1/2}\Omega_A^{\top} \); it is isotropic on \( T_{BA}\mathcal M_r \) with \( \mathbb E\|\mathcal P(\Xi)\|_F^2=r(d_{in}+d_{out}-r) \), independent of \( \|A\|_F,\|B\|_F \). The noisy step is post-processed by right/left rank-space preconditioners \( (V+\lambda I_r)^{-1/2} \) built from \( r\times r \) second moments, with floors \( \lambda\asymp(\sigma C/b)^2\,\mathrm{tr}(\cdot^{-1})/r \), and then retracted to rank \( r \) by truncated SVD. Because the step is additive in the tangent space, the bilinear noise term \( \eta^2\xi_B\xi_A \) of factor-space DP never appears, and the retraction error is \( O(\eta^2) \).
methods.mergeable_reason: The released adapter is an ordinary low-rank product and merges like LoRA; privacy follows from post-processing. Because the official code trains on a spectrally re-based base \( W_{res}=W_0-U_r\Sigma_rV_r^{\top} \), it saves the adapter re-expressed against the original \( W_0 \) as the rank-\( 2r \) pair \( [B,\,B_0]\,[A;\,-A_0] \) (PiSSA-style conversion in spectral_rebase_adapter_inplace), which merges into \( W_0 \) the same way.
methods.identity_at_init: The paper does not state an init. The tangent projectors and noise sampler need full-column-rank \( B \) and full-row-rank \( A \), which rules out LoRA's \( B=0 \). The official code uses a PiSSA-style spectral residual init, \( W_0\leftarrow W_0-U_r\Sigma_rV_r^{\top} \), \( B=U_r(\Sigma_r/s)^{1/2} \), \( A=(\Sigma_r/s)^{1/2}V_r^{\top} \) with LoRA scale \( s \), so \( W_{res}+sBA \) equals the original \( W_0 \) at step 0 (function-preserving with non-degenerate factors).
methods.key_idea: LoRA factors are defined only up to \( (B,A)\mapsto(BR,R^{-1}A) \), so DP-SGD on the factors clips and noises a gauge-dependent quantity and injects a bilinear \( \eta^2\xi_B\xi_A \) term whose energy can be made arbitrarily large without changing \( BA \). PRISM clips and noises the projection of per-example gradients onto the tangent space of the rank-\( r \) manifold at \( BA \), which gives gauge-invariant updates with closed-form intrinsic noise \( \tfrac{\sigma C}{b}\sqrt{r(d_{in}+d_{out}-r)} \).
methods.results_note: On GLUE8 and Math-10K with Gemma-3-4B-pt, PRISM has the best average utility under DP (0.690 at epsilon=6 and 0.680 at epsilon=3, delta=1e-5) against FFA-LoRA, LoRA-RITE, AdamW, LoRA+ and LAMB, while LoRA-RITE is best without DP.

relations.note: same adapter; only the private optimisation of the factors changes
FFA-LoRA freezes \( A \) so DP noise enters as \( \xi_BA_0 \) with no bilinear term, but its size still depends on the frozen factor's norm; PRISM removes that dependence; DP baseline

LoRA-RITE makes a deterministic optimizer transformation-invariant; PRISM argues this does not make the randomized clip-and-noise step invariant and extends invariance to it, while also using \( r\times r \) rank-space second moments; baseline (best without DP)

structural kinship, not cited: PRISM's canonical lift starts from the scaled gradients \( g_B(AA^{\top})^{\dagger} \) and \( (B^{\top}B)^{\dagger}g_A \) of Riemannian-preconditioned LoRA and subtracts half the overlap term; both rest on the quotient geometry of fixed-rank matrices (PRISM cites Mishra et al. 2014, not Zhang and Pilanci)

methods.name: KeepLoRA
methods.full_name: KeepLoRA: residual-subspace gradient adaptation for continual learning
methods.paper_title: KeepLoRA: Continual Learning with Residual Gradient Adaptation
methods.formula_latex: W_0=U_0\Sigma_0V_0^{\top},\ P_W=V_{0,[:,1:p]}\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{in}\times p}\ \big(\text{smallest }p\text{ with }\|\Sigma_{0,[1:p]}\|_F^2\ge\epsilon_w\|W_0\|_F^2\big);\ \ \hat G_t=G_t\big(I-P_WP_W^{\top}-M_{t-1}M_{t-1}^{\top}\big),\ G_t=\nabla_W\mathcal{L}(W;\mathcal{D}^t)\ \text{at the first step};\ \ \hat G_t=USV^{\top}:\ A_t=V_{[:,1:r]}^{\top}\ (\text{frozen}),\ B_t^{(0)}=U_{[:,1:r]}S_{[1:r]};\ \ W=W'+\tfrac{\alpha}{r}B_tA_t,\ W'=W-\tfrac{\alpha}{r}B_t^{(0)}A_t\ \text{frozen},\ B_t\ \text{trained}\ \Rightarrow\ \Delta W=-\tfrac{\eta\alpha^2}{r^2}\,G\,A_t^{\top}A_t;\ \ \text{after task }t:\ W\leftarrow W'+\tfrac{\alpha}{r}B_tA_t,\ M_t=[M_{t-1},\ \text{top-}m\ \text{directions in }\mathbb{R}^{d_{in}}\text{ of }(I-P_WP_W^{\top}-M_{t-1}M_{t-1}^{\top})X_t]\ (m\text{ set by energy threshold }\epsilon_f)
methods.trainable_params: r\,d_{out}\ \text{per adapted matrix per task (only }B_t\text{; }A_t\text{ frozen)}
methods.locus: Linear (attention) weight matrices of CLIP ViT-B/16 image and text encoders and of LLaVA's language model; the constraint acts on the input side \( \mathbb R^{d_{in}} \) of each adapted matrix.
methods.structure: Per task, a LoRA with frozen down-projection \( A_t \) whose rows span a subspace of the residual space \( \{P_W,M_{t-1}\}^{\perp}\subset\mathbb R^{d_{in}} \). \( P_W \) holds the principal input-side singular vectors of the pre-trained weight (general knowledge) and \( M_{t-1} \) the dominant input-feature directions of past tasks. \( A_t \) is the top-\( r \) right singular subspace of the first-step gradient after projecting out \( [P_W,M_{t-1}] \), and \( B_t \) starts at \( U_{[:,1:r]}S_{[1:r]} \) with \( W'=W-\tfrac{\alpha}{r}B_t^{(0)}A_t \) absorbing the offset. Training only \( B_t \) makes every step a projected gradient step \( \Delta W\propto-GA_t^{\top}A_t \) (Prop. 3.1), so \( \Delta W\,[P_W,M_{t-1}]=0 \): outputs on old-task feature directions and on the principal input subspace of the pre-trained weight are untouched. After each task the adapter is merged and \( M \) grows, with \( p+k\le d_{in} \) bounding the stored memory. KeepLoRA+ adds trainable class prototypes for CLIP classification.
methods.mergeable_reason: Each task's \( \tfrac{\alpha}{r}B_tA_t \) is merged into \( W \) after training (Algorithm 1), so inference uses a single dense matrix with no task identity and no extra modules (KeepLoRA+ keeps its class prototypes).
methods.identity_at_init: Yes, by re-basing: \( B_t^{(0)}A_t\ne0 \), but the frozen weight is replaced by \( W'=W-\tfrac{\alpha}{r}B_t^{(0)}A_t \), so \( W'+\tfrac{\alpha}{r}B_t^{(0)}A_t=W \) at the start of every task.
methods.key_idea: General knowledge sits in the principal singular subspace of the pre-trained weights and task knowledge in the residual subspace, so KeepLoRA initialises each task's LoRA from the SVD of the first-step gradient projected away from both that principal subspace and past-task feature directions, then freezes \( A_t \). Training only \( B_t \) turns every update into gradient descent confined to the residual subspace, which balances retention of pre-trained knowledge, retention of past tasks and plasticity.

methods.structure: No adapter: the weight step is the usual full-rank Adam (or Muon) step, but the EMA momenta are stored as rank-\( r \) factors. The EMA update \( m\leftarrow\beta m+(1-\beta)g \) is one gradient step with learning rate \( 1-\beta \) on \( \tfrac12\|m-g\|_F^2 \), so momentum is the weight of an online linear regressor. LoRA-Pre replaces \( m \) by \( m_Bm_A \) and takes one exact Newton step per factor on \( \tfrac12\|m_Bm_A-g\|_F^2 \) (Hessians \( m_Am_A^{\top}\otimes I \) and \( I\otimes m_B^{\top}m_B \)). The result is a simultaneous (Jacobi-style) EMA of each factor toward the least-squares fit of the new gradient given the other factor's previous value, with \( 1-\gamma_1=\sqrt{\beta_1} \) so that the product decays at Adam's rate \( \beta_1 \). The second moment stays positive through the Hadamard-square parametrisation \( v=(v_Bv_A)^{\circ2} \), with \( v_Bv_A \) regressed onto \( |g| \). For Muon the regression target is \( \tfrac12\|m-g\|_F^2-\tfrac{\mu}{1-\mu}\langle m,g\rangle \). Since the Adam ratio \( \hat M_t/\sqrt{\hat V_t} \) is elementwise, the weight update is full-rank even though the state is rank-\( r \). LoRA's update is rank-\( r \), and GaLore's step lies in a rank-\( r \) projected subspace. Adafactor's rank-1 factored second moment is an earlier instance of factoring optimizer state.
methods.mergeable_reason: There is no auxiliary module: updates are written straight into W, so the result is an ordinary dense checkpoint with the original architecture and unchanged inference cost.
methods.identity_at_init: Trivial: no reparametrisation, training starts at \( W_0 \) (random init for pre-training). The factored states start at \( m_B=v_B=0 \), \( m_A,v_A\sim\mathcal N(0,0.02) \), so the reconstructed momenta start at 0 as in Adam. Theorem 3.1 assumes full-rank factors and Algorithm 1 writes plain inverses, which are singular at the first step because \( m_{B,0}=0 \). Appendix C.1 defines the update with Tikhonov-damped pseudo-inverses \( (m_B^{\top}m_B+\lambda_d I)^{-1}m_B^{\top} \) and \( m_A^{\top}(m_Am_A^{\top}+\lambda_d I)^{-1} \), \( \lambda_d>0 \), which are well defined at \( m_B=0 \); the value of \( \lambda_d \) used in experiments is not reported and the code is not released.
methods.key_idea: An EMA momentum update is one step of online gradient descent on \( \tfrac12\|m-g\|_F^2 \), so momentum is an online linear regressor and can be compressed like any model. LoRA-Pre factors \( m \) (and \( v=(v_Bv_A)^{\circ2} \)) into rank-\( r \) matrices updated by closed-form Newton steps, which cuts optimizer memory for Adam and Muon in both pre-training and fine-tuning.
methods.results_note: Pre-training Llama-1B on C4 at rank 512, LoRA-Pre Adam reaches 13.53 validation perplexity versus 15.64 for GaLore and 15.56 for full-state Adam, and fine-tuning on MetaMath100k at rank 8 it beats LoRA by 3.14 points on Llama-3.1-8B and 6.17 points on Llama-2-7B (GSM8K/MATH-500 average).

methods.structure: LoRA with a learned diagonal gate between the factors, \( B\,\mathrm{diag}(m)\,A \): a sparsifying selector over the \( r \) rank-one directions, like SoRA's gate but trained with a variational-IB KL to a Bernoulli prior. A training-time map across layers is added on top: the vectorised filtered updates \( U=[u_1;\dots;u_L] \) pass through a shallow residual GCN on a depth graph (adjacent layers plus semantic edges between layers with highly aligned updates or gradients). To first order this is a Laplacian smoothing step \( U\leftarrow U-\eta(\mathbf L\otimes I)U \), which lowers the drift energy \( \sum_l\|u_{l+1}-u_l\|^2 \). Section 3.3 and the released code merge the coordinated \( \Delta\tilde W_l^{\mathrm{final}} \), which in general no longer has rank \( \le r \) because the GCN mixes and nonlinearly maps updates from several layers. Appendix E.7 says instead that the gated \( \Delta\tilde W \) is merged. The released code's coordinator is a dense linear encoder on \( \mathrm{vec}(\Delta\tilde W_l) \) of width \( d_{out}d_{in} \), which does not match the stated \( <0.05\% \) overhead at LLaMA scale.

The paper does not discuss this.
methods.key_idea: Not all \( r \) LoRA directions carry task signal, and layers adapted independently drift apart. StructLoRA gates the rank-one directions with an information-bottleneck filter and, during training only, smooths the per-layer updates across depth with a shallow GCN (a Laplacian smoother), then merges the result so inference costs the same as LoRA.

So the optimal LR shrinks as \( r^{-1/2} \) for \( \alpha=1 \) and as \( r^{-1/4} \) for rsLoRA's \( \alpha=r^{-1/2} \), and is rank-invariant for \( \alpha=r^{-1} \) (standard \( \alpha/r \)), though with a narrow stable range. papers.claim: For \( W=W_0+\tfrac{\alpha}{r}BA \), a step decomposes exactly into a signal \( \tfrac{\alpha}{r}(B\Delta A+\Delta B\,A) \) and a bilinear drift \( \tfrac{\alpha}{r}\Delta B\,\Delta A \). The parameter Hessian splits likewise into \( J^{\top}H_\ell J\succeq0 \) and an indefinite structural term. At LoRA init (\( B=0 \), \( A_{ij}\sim\mathcal N(0,\sigma_A^2) \)) the signal curvature is suppressed, \( \mathbb E\,\mathrm{Tr}\,\mathcal H_{\mathrm{Signal}}=\alpha^2(\sigma_A^2/r)\,\mathrm{Tr}\,H_\ell \), so full-FT hyperparameters are overly conservative. Under Adam the signal scales as \( \alpha\eta \) and the drift as \( \alpha\eta^2 \): raising \( \alpha \) accelerates without degrading the signal-to-drift ratio \( \Theta(1/\eta) \), while raising \( \eta \) degrades it, so \( \alpha \) and \( \eta \) are not interchangeable. Matching curvature to full FT gives \( \alpha=\Theta(\sqrt r/\sigma_A) \). Empirically \( \alpha^*\approx C\sqrt r \) with \( C\approx256 \) (Llama-3-1B, Tulu-3), 512 (8B) and 1024 (OpenThoughts). LoRA-\( \alpha \) sets \( \Delta W=\tfrac{\alpha\,\alpha_{base}}{r}BA \) with \( \alpha_{base}=256\sqrt r \) (or \( \sqrt r/\sigma_A \)) and uses the full-FT learning rate.

papers.title: Uniform Spectral Growth and Convergence of Muon in LoRA-Style Matrix Factorization
papers.venue: NeurIPS 2026 (poster; accepted as 'Uniform Spectral Growth under Factor-wise Muon Orthogonalization in Matrix Factorization and LoRA')
papers.claim: For \( \min_{B,A}\tfrac12\|BA-Y\|_F^2 \) from LoRA-style init (output-side factor \( B(0)=0 \), input-side factor \( A(0)=\gamma N \) small Gaussian), spectral gradient flow orthogonalises each factor's gradient separately with \( \mathcal T_\beta(M)=(MM^{\top}+\beta I)^{-1/2}M \). Under this flow the core product stays near-diagonal (\( O(\gamma) \) off-diagonal), and the square roots of all active singular values of \( BA \) grow at unit rate, \( \tfrac{d}{dt}\sqrt{d_i}=1+O(\varepsilon^{1/4}) \). So the smallest target singular value is reached first, the opposite of plain gradient flow's largest-first, saddle-to-saddle learning. For almost all inits the flow converges to a global minimum (the best rank-\( r \) approximation of \( Y \)) or the factor norms diverge; with \( \ell_2 \) regularisation convergence is global. The balancedness quantity \( B^{\top}B-AA^{\top} \) conserved by plain gradient flow need not be conserved here. Near-uniform growth is also observed with Newton-Schulz Muon in LoRA fine-tuning of LLMs.
papers.relevance: Extends the catalogued gradient-flow papers (lora-gradient-flow-matrix-factorization, implicit-regularization-deep-matrix-factorization, conservation-laws-gradient-flows) to Muon-type optimizers. Factor-wise orthogonalisation can break the conservation law tied to LoRA's \( GL(r) \) symmetry and replaces the incremental (largest-first, saddle-to-saddle) learning of plain gradient flow with equal-rate growth in \( \sqrt{\sigma_i} \), so arguments that rely on largest-first ordering do not carry over to factor-wise Muon. It also cautions that uniform growth amplifies all \( r \) directions, which can hurt when the useful update has rank below \( r \).

papers.title: Weight Updates as Activation Shifts: A Principled Framework for Steering
papers.claim: For a GLU MLP \( W_d(\phi(W_gh)\odot W_uh) \), a first-order input perturbation \( \Delta h \) reproduces the first-order effect of perturbing \( W_g,W_u \) but misses the down-projection term \( (\Delta W_d)m \), which a post-MLP additive edit can absorb. With the fine-tuned hidden state as an oracle target, the MLP output accounts for only 40-70% of the block-output magnitude across layers (Llama-3.2, Winogrande), so a post-MLP edit misses the attention and skip-connection share. A theorem gives the best linear post-block approximation of post-MLP steering in terms of principal angles between sample-space singular subspaces. A post-block bottleneck adapter \( h\mapsto h+W_2\phi(W_1h) \) (after the skip connection) at every layer comes within 0.2-0.9% of full SFT accuracy with 0.04% of parameters and beats ReFT and LoRA. Weight and activation updates express different function classes, and joint training with \( W_2\leftarrow(I-VV^{\top})W_2 \), \( V \) an orthonormal basis of \( \mathrm{col}(B_{\mathrm{LoRA}}) \), beats either alone by up to 3.8%.
papers.relevance: A formal bridge between the activation-editing locus (loreft, red, road; representation-engineering, inference-time-intervention) and the weight locus (lora): to first order a weight update on the MLP is an activation shift, except for the output-projection term, and the post-block residual stream is where the activation locus can absorb it. It explains why ReFT-style residual-stream edits work, it is the same locus PreFT's \( \text{DiReFT}_P \) uses, and its orthogonality-constrained joint adapter is a hybrid entry point between the two loci.
corrections: claim: the 40-70% figure is the ratio of MLP-output norm to block-output norm (Sec. 3.3, Figs. 2-3), not a measured fraction of the oracle change recovered by post-MLP edits. Rephrased.
relevance: 'steering' is not a catalogue id. It is replaced by the existing paper ids representation-engineering and inference-time-intervention. DiReFT_P is wrapped in \( \).

papers.title: Diffract: Spectral View of LLM Domain Adaptation
papers.claim: On OLMo 2 (1B, 7B, 13B, plus released 32B checkpoints), continual pre-training on math, instruction, code and text leaves the singular-value spectra of the weights almost unchanged. Adaptation happens mainly through singular-vector changes concentrated near spectral peaks of attention matrices. Attention heads become heterogeneous as the pre-training budget grows. A head-importance criterion (CPT-delta Frobenius norms relative to a text-CPT reference) lets up to 60% of head updates be rewound to pre-trained values without measurable loss, and rewinding about 15% of heads raises math accuracy by up to 4% (7B). Dropping the smallest singular values of the CPT delta costs no measurable GSM8K accuracy up to 50% of them for 7B and 70% for 13B (1B deltas are less compressible), and linear interpolation between CPT checkpoints of different domains is smooth ('domain connectivity').
papers.relevance: Full-parameter CPT evidence on the shape of useful updates; it is not a PEFT method. Fixed spectra with rotating singular vectors are the signature of multiplicative orthogonal updates (oft, boft, goft preserve the singular values of \( W_0 \) exactly). A one-sided rotation changes the singular vectors on one side only, and the paper measures agreement of left singular vectors only (App. A.3), so it does not settle whether the observed rotations are one- or two-sided. The same finding cuts against value-only spectral tuning (svf), which cannot rotate singular vectors, so the seed's reading of it as support for SVF/SVFT/PiSSA/MiLoRA needs this qualification. The delta-truncation result supports low-rank compressibility of adaptation deltas (lora). Head rewind is selective sparsity at head granularity, and domain connectivity supports linear merging of domain deltas (task-arithmetic).
corrections: claim: SVD-truncation tolerance is 50% of singular values for 7B and 70% for 13B (Sec. 4.4, Fig. 5); 1B degrades about 10% after 30% truncation. The old 'up to 50%' understated the 13B result and omitted the 1B caveat.

papers.title: The Appeal and Reality of Recycling LoRAs with Adaptive Merging
papers.claim: The study uses a pool of 958 user-contributed Hugging Face LoRAs for Llama 3.1 8B-Instruct and 62 target tasks with 100 labelled examples each. Adaptive merging (LoraHub, \( \pi \)-Tuning, AdaMerging, and a new method found by a design-space search) beats the base model but gives limited benefit over simply training a target-task LoRA on the same 100 examples (80 train, 20 validation); non-adaptive merges with fixed uniform coefficients (averaging, TIES, TSV) underperform the adaptive ones. Arrow, a zero-shot per-token router, is grouped with the non-adaptive methods in Fig. 2, although Sec. 4 lists it with the adaptive ones. When the target-task LoRA is in the pool, which recycled LoRAs are chosen hardly matters, and LoRAs with random parameter values work about as well. This points to a regularisation effect rather than positive transfer. Positive transfer does appear with a bespoke pool of highly relevant, consistently trained LoRAs.
papers.relevance: An empirical counterweight for the composition family (lorahub, arrow, adamerging, ties-merging, tsv-merge): reported gains from merging adapters largely reflect curated, task-relevant pools. In atlas terms, a composition operator on adapter space adds task information only when the pool contains relevant modules; otherwise it acts as a regulariser on the target-task adapter. PHATGOOSE-style routing is not evaluated, so that extension of the conclusion is untested.
corrections: claim: Arrow was listed as an adaptive merging method. It tunes no coefficients on target data, and the paper's Fig. 2 caption groups it with the non-adaptive methods (Sec. 4's text is inconsistent). Also added the 80/20 split of the 100 examples.

papers.title: Learning Dynamics of Zeroth-Order Optimization: A Kernel Perspective
papers.claim: One step of multi-perturbation ZO-SGD (two-point estimator, \( P \) perturbations) changes model log-probabilities through a projected eNTK \( \mathcal K(x_o,x_u;U)=\nabla_\theta z(x_o)^{\top}UU^{\top}\nabla_\theta z(x_u) \), with \( U\in\mathbb R^{d\times P} \) the stacked normalised perturbations. By an inner-product Johnson-Lindenstrauss lemma the kernel error is \( \epsilon=O(\sqrt{\ln V/P}) \), so the gap between ZO and first-order one-step dynamics is \( \lesssim\sqrt{V\log V/P} \) times model-dependent factors. This depends on the output size \( V \), not the parameter count \( d \), which explains ZO fine-tuning's success without the low-effective-rank Hessian assumption. Gaussian and Rademacher perturbations behave alike, and fidelity improves as \( O(1/\sqrt P) \) (validated on LeNet/MNIST and OPT-125M to 1.3B on SST-2).
papers.relevance: Extends kernel-view-lm-finetuning, which used a JL argument to show LoRA preserves the SGD fine-tuning kernel, to zeroth-order training. In both, a random low-dimensional projection approximately preserves the eNTK: ZO (mezo, zo-bench) redraws the projection every step in parameter space, while LoRA-style subspace training fixes one. This gives a common kernel-level account of the ZO entries alongside MeZO.

The paper frames the result as an alternative to the low-effective-rank Hessian assumption of Malladi et al., as the claim says. Ids in the relevance (mezo, zo-bench, kernel-view-lm-finetuning) exist.

papers.title: Understanding LoRA as Knowledge Memory: An Empirical Analysis
papers.claim: Rank sweeps from 2 to 1024 with knowledge loads of 1K-20K tokens on Llama-3.1-8B and Qwen3-8B (PhoneBook key-value pairs, CounterFact edits) show that LoRA's memorisation capacity grows with rank but saturates at a rank-dependent load. Knowledge stored per trainable parameter peaks at low rank (around r=4). Among synthetic formats (QA, summary, rewrite), QA pairs give the largest gains and the best token-efficiency, mixing formats helps further, and a stronger generator (GPT-4.1 versus Llama-3.1-8B) helps. In multi-LoRA systems, top-1 embedding routing can underperform one LoRA holding everything, and merging the top-k retrieved modules trades routing errors against interference: TIES is best, and vanilla concatenation collapses mainly through scale mismatch: rescaling each factor by \( 1/\sqrt N \) recovers most of the gap to linear averaging. LoRA memory works best alongside RAG or ICL rather than replacing them.
papers.relevance: Updates the 2025 lora-knowledge-capacity entry with capacity curves, rank-efficiency measurements and multi-module composition. It is empirical analysis, not theory. It treats rank as a capacity knob (cf. lora-learns-less-forgets-less) and gives composition evidence relevant to document- and knowledge-module methods (doc-to-lora, text-to-lora, loraretriever, lorahub), including the calibration fact that concatenated adapters need \( 1/\sqrt N \) factor scaling.
corrections: claim: 'synthetic QA rewrites' merged two distinct formats. The paper finds QA best per token, rewrite and summary helpful in mixtures, and generator quality important (Q4, Q5, Q7). Rephrased.
claim: 'fails only through scale mismatch' overstated Q10, which says 1/sqrt(N) rescaling 'recovers most of the gap to Linear'. Rephrased, and 1/sqrt(N) is wrapped in \( \) in claim and relevance.

notes: All 6 seed methods and all 8 seed papers exist on arXiv under the given ids; none is a duplicate of a catalogued method and none was skipped. Formulas were taken from each paper's method section (arXiv HTML full text) and rewritten in catalogue notation (\( W_0\in\mathbb R^{d_{out}\times d_{in}} \), \( \Delta W=BA \), \( A \) down, \( B \) up). Several papers use the transposed convention: OrthoMerge writes \( W=RW_0 \) with \( W_0\in\mathbb R^{d_{in}\times d_{out}} \), PRISM writes \( Z=AB^{\top} \), KeepLoRA and StructLoRA write \( y=x(W+AB) \) or \( W_0+AB \) with \( A \) as the up/down factor swapped, and the Muon paper puts the zero-initialised factor on the left. Procrustes, projectors and inits were converted, and the conversions were checked algebraically (for example PRISM's lift satisfies \( \Delta B\,A+B\,\Delta A=\mathcal P_{B,A}(G) \)). Venues were verified on official lists: NeurIPS 2026 orals-posters JSON (PreFT poster; scaling-factor paper poster; Muon paper poster under the title 'Uniform Spectral Growth under Factor-wise Muon Orthogonalization in Matrix Factorization and LoRA'), ICML 2026 JSON (OrthoMerge, muA, steering, recycling, ZO-kernel and LoRA-memory posters; PRISM and Diffract 'Accept (spotlight)' with oral events), ICLR 2026 JSON (KeepLoRA poster, LoRA-Pre Oral) and the ACL Anthology (StructLoRA = 2026.acl-long.97). None of the six methods is in Hugging Face PEFT as of v0.21.2 (2026-10-01): no tuner directory, merge_utils function or release note matches. Corrections to the seed descriptions: (1) muA: the seed says the optimal LR is rank-invariant or scales as \( 1/r \). Corollary 4.4 gives \( \eta=\Theta(n^{-1/2}r^{-(1-\gamma)/2}) \) for Init[A] with \( \alpha=r^{-\gamma} \): \( r^{-1/2} \) at \( \alpha=1 \), \( r^{-1/4} \) for rsLoRA, rank-invariant at \( \alpha=1/r \). Init[B] with \( \alpha=1 \) gives rank-invariant \( \Theta(1/n) \) matching full FT. The abstract's word 'inversely' is loose. (2) Diffract studies full-parameter continual pre-training of OLMo 2, not PEFT. Its central finding (spectra fixed, singular vectors rotate) supports multiplicative orthogonal methods (OFT family) more than SVF, which only rescales singular values; the relevance text says so. (3) PreFT's token-time locus is not entirely new to the atlas: alora (Activated LoRA, in verified/hf-peft.json) gates the same LoRA update by position in the mirror-image way, and PreFT cites it. A dual-to edge preft -> alora was added. PreFT's title differs slightly between the arXiv abstract page ('for efficient inference', used here) and the HTML/NeurIPS listing ('for inference efficiency'). (4) PRISM's paper does not state an init. The official code uses a PiSSA-style spectral residual init because the tangent projectors need full-rank factors; this is recorded in identity_at_init. (5) LoRA-Pre is a full-parameter memory-efficient optimizer, not an adapter: weight updates are full-rank and only the momenta are rank-r. Its GitHub repo contains only a README ('code release coming soon'), so code_url points to a placeholder. Algorithm 1 writes plain inverses, which are singular at step 1 because \( m_{B,0}=0 \); Appendix C.1 states the update with Tikhonov-damped pseudo-inverses (\( \lambda>0 \)), but the experimental \( \lambda \) is not reported. (6) StructLoRA has medium confidence. The paper is internally inconsistent about which update is merged (Sec. 3.3 says the GNN output \( \Delta\tilde W^{final} \), App. E.7 says the gated \( \Delta\tilde W \)). The released repo is a 'scaffold' whose coordinator has a dense encoder of width \( d_{out}d_{in} \), incompatible with the stated <0.05% overhead at LLaMA scale, and adds bias terms that make the coordinated update nonzero at init. The deployed update is therefore not guaranteed to be rank \( \le r \). (7) KeepLoRA does not 'project the gradient during training' in a separate optimizer. It initialises a frozen \( A_t \) from the SVD of the projected first-step gradient and trains only \( B_t \), which by its Prop. 3.1 makes every update a projected gradient step. It cites GPM and InfLoRA but not LoRA-GA, LoRA-FA or MiLoRA; edges to lora-ga and lora-fa are labelled as uncited structural analogues. (8) OrthoMerge's 'Lie algebra' map is the inverse Cayley transform, not the matrix logarithm, so averaging is done in Cayley coordinates. The Cayley chart excludes orthogonal matrices with eigenvalue -1 (for example Procrustes reflections), a case the paper does not discuss. Its arXiv comment still says 'Technical report' although it is an ICML 2026 poster. (9) The recycling paper's arXiv comment says 'Preprint', but it is in the ICML 2026 accepted list. It evaluates LoraHub, \( \pi \)-Tuning, AdaMerging, simple averaging, TIES, TSV and the zero-shot router Arrow, but not PHATGOOSE. (10) LoRA-as-knowledge-memory is empirical and filed as analysis (an update of lora-knowledge-capacity), not as theory. Relations point only to existing method ids (as in the rest of the catalogue, where no relation targets a paper id); uncited structural analogues are marked in the edge notes. Semantic Scholar was not queried, and the seed citation counts were not re-verified.
verification_summary: Adversarial verification on 2026-10-02 of 6 methods and 8 papers. All 14 verified; none dropped. Existence and metadata: all 14 arXiv ids were confirmed by a batch arXiv API query (after 503/429 retries) and by the abs pages. Titles, first authors and first-version dates (all 2026, from 2601.19659 on 2026-01-27 to 2608.10850 on 2026-08-11) match. Venues confirmed on primary sources: icml-2026-orals-posters.json (OrthoMerge, muA, steering, recycling, ZO-kernel and LoRA-memory are 'Accept (regular)' posters; PRISM and Diffract are 'Accept (spotlight)' with oral events), iclr-2026-orals-posters.json (KeepLoRA poster, LoRA-Pre oral), neurips-2026-orals-posters.json (PreFT, the scaling-factor paper and the Muon paper, the last under its NeurIPS title) and the ACL Anthology (StructLoRA = 2026.acl-long.97). Formulas were re-derived from each paper's method section (arXiv HTML), with the transposed conventions of OrthoMerge, PRISM, KeepLoRA, StructLoRA and the Muon paper converted symbol by symbol. Released code was read for PreFT, PRISM, KeepLoRA and StructLoRA. HF PEFT: none of the six methods is in huggingface/peft main (v0.21.2, 2026-10-01). There is no tuner directory, merge_utils function, optimizers/ entry or release-note mention. Every relation target is an existing method id, every prose-named id exists, and none of the 14 ids or arXiv numbers collides with existing_index.json or the sibling addendum2026 batches. 22 corrections were recorded. Substantive: (1) LoRA-Pre: Appendix C.1 does regularise the inverse (Tikhonov-damped pseudo-inverses), contrary to the seed note, and the factor updates are simultaneous, not alternating. (2) PRISM: the official code saves the adapter re-based to the original W_0 as a rank-2r pair. (3) PreFT: the S-LoRA edge changed from competes-with to combines; App. A.2 vs C.1 disagree on which DiReFT factor is zero at init. (4) StructLoRA: the gate relaxation and prior now separate paper from code. (5) OrthoMerge: the TSV-M+OrthoMerge-C result was attributed to the -G variant. (6) Scaling-factor paper: the 16x-256x ratio depends on rank, not a constant. (7) Steering paper: 40-70% is an MLP-to-block norm ratio, and 'steering' was not an id. (8) Diffract: the truncation tolerance is 50% for 7B and 70% for 13B, and the vector agreement covers left singular vectors only. (9) Recycling: Arrow is a zero-shot router, not an adaptive merge. (10) LoRA memory: the synthetic-format and concatenation claims were rephrased to match the paper. (11) Muon paper: removed an unsupported PiSSA-motivation claim. The remaining fixes wrap math fragments in \( \). Semantic Scholar was not queried; citation counts are not part of this file.
